item.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
item.description: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Financial trading makes this limitation especially consequential: prices, news, market conditions, portfolio positions, and available capital evolve continuously. item.description: The increasing aquatic Internet of Things (AIoTs) require computational support and coverage in applications such as maritime search and rescue. item.title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation
item.description: High-quality causal reasoning datasets are essential for developing models with reliable causal understanding, particularly in specialized domains. However, existing datasets frequently suffer from incorrect annotations and structural imbalances, which can lead to biased predictions and limited generalization. item.description: This paper presents a framework for computer-aided music composition and performance based on quantum reinforcement learning and multi-agent interaction. item.description: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without sharing datasets. However, existing federated learning methods for autonomous driving typically require multi-round communication and lack closed-loop evaluation, while one-shot methods mainly focus on perception tasks. item.description: Automated red teaming is essential for identifying safety failures in large language models (LLMs), but its practical scalability depends on the resources required to discover those failures. item.description: Safe reinforcement learning (RL) aims to prevent agents from taking actions that are dangerous or destructive to their environment. item.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
item.description: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. item.title: OMNIS+: Semantic RAN Slicing and Quantization for Dynamic Split Neural Networks
item.description: Edge computing enables resource-constrained devices to execute machine learning (ML) applications via task offloading, with radio access network (RAN) slicing playing a crucial role in provisioning joint communication and computing resources. item.title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting
item.description: Forecasting future hand movements from egocentric videos plays an important role in understanding human intentions and hand-object interactions. However, different manipulation intentions can lead to substantially different hand trajectories even when interacting with the same object. item.title: PGU-Decoder: Prior-Guided Unified Decoding for Industrial Road-Network Map Updating
item.description: Timely road-network map updates are essential to navigation and autonomous driving. Three key tasks are intra-intersection road network generation, merging/diverging detection, and drivable-area detection, covering topology, geometry, and attributes, respectively. Separate pipelines duplicate rule maintenance, quality assurance, and manual verification, increasing operational costs. We propose PGU-Decoder, a production-grade unified decoding framework for semantic prediction across these tasks.

item.description: Large-scale multi-mobile-robot systems require fast and reliable path planning under realistic motion constraints. item.description: Radio Access Network (RAN) slicing is a shared resource allocation problem: each slice seeks to satisfy its Service Level Agreement (SLA) with minimal radio-resource consumption, while all slices compete for a limited resource budget. item.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
item.description: Video evaluators play an important role in video generation, yet they miss motion defects, limiting the quality of generated videos.
